arguments.prompt: Repaint the TWO DOGS' BODY SURFACES in FIRST image, the bazaar bangle scene. Preserve all anatomy, body proportions, faces, expressions, ears, paws, exact poses, bangle position and full market composition. Neet left leans to nudge bangle rim with one paw, three support feet; Buddy right politely lifts one forepaw with three support feet. IMPORTANT STYLE CORRECTION: replace EVERY looping fur mark and engraved texture on both dogs torso, shoulders, hips, neck and legs with FLAT CLEAN COLOR SHAPES and a few broad smooth shading planes. Match the completely flat torso paint shown by dogs in SECOND image (park illustration). Use second image ONLY for flat body finish, never anatomy/composition/scale; DO NOT ADD its third dog or scenery. These are very short coats: zero internal hairs, wavy lines, curls, dashes, hatching, grain or embossed pattern on body color fields. Smooth continuous body edges. Neet body golden fawn with cream bib/muzzle, tiny nub tail; Buddy dark charcoal with tan chest and pale distal legs. Preserve Buddy regional furnished muzzle/brows/ears, but no shaggy neck/back/flank. Third and fourth images are original photo anatomical identity anchors, only visible regions, no measured ratios. N19 short smooth Neet, B29 moderately elongated Buddy and true clearance; B29 stride not a neutral measurement. Preserve the narrative state and all supports, elegant restrained expressions. No text. Keep detailed watercolor bazaar behind simplified flat painted bodies. Repaint broadly rather than filtering or blurring the existing curly texture.
